## Minimum bar (every sprint)

No merged PRs, no sprint report, or no release → the whole team gets **0** for the sprint.

## Sprint report (`docs/sprintN/report.md`, or .pdf/.docx), team deliverable

Sections (S1 format, carried forward): Team (name, members + GitHub usernames, project, repo link) · Sprint overview (goals, what was actually delivered, honest scope changes) · Sprint backlog (milestone link + table: title, owner, points, scope, status) · Requirements & design (specs done before coding? surprises, key decisions) · Completed issues (table: issue, owner, PRs w/ link/author/reviewers/status, change summary) · Test strategy (test types; what couldn't be auto-tested and why) · AI tool usage (per member: tools, session count, folder link, 2–3 sentences on what worked or should change, patterns vs. previous sprint) · Release (tag + link) · Risks & retrospective · Next-sprint plan (ideas + carryovers).

- S2 added: Sprint 1 carryovers section, UML + check-in entries in the deliverables summary.
- S3 adds: **Suite health** (baseline table per relevant suite: command/CI workflow + passed/failed/skipped at the `-csci435-s2` tag AND at sprint end; failures grouped by cause with one linked issue per cause; no team-introduced failures; skipped tests and disabled checks need a linked issue + a reason in a code comment), links to every member's mutation-testing file, hardening issues + their sources, carryovers.
- Must **render on GitHub**: no escaped `\|` or `\[` in tables/links. Write fresh sections, don't copy the old report. Vague bullets earn nothing; be specific with links.

## Release (team)

- Never bump the version. Tag = the same base version + `-csci435-s<N>` (e.g. `v2.17.2-csci435-s3`). `git tag v<ver>-csci435-sN && git push origin v<ver>-csci435-sN`, then create a GitHub Release from it.
- Description summarizes features, fixes, improvements (S3: also hardening), not just the tag name. S3: create it **after the last Sprint 3 merge** so it matches final `master`.
- Look up the previous sprint's tag to get the base version (`git tag -l '*csci435*'`).

## Milestones

Each sprint needs a GitHub milestone named exactly `Sprint N` with all selected issues (S3: and code PRs) attached; each issue has exactly one assignee, and every member owns at least one.

## Mid-sprint check-in (individual)

`docs/sprintN/checkin/<username>.md`. S3 questions (~100 words each): what's implemented so far and what remains; one thing learned about testing in the project; one risk to finishing by Nov 19 and the plan for it. **Must link at least one code PR authored by the student that is open and ready for review, or merged, by Nov 12.**

See also [[course-pr-requirements]], [[course-issue-requirements]], [[course-ai-log-rules]], [[course-sprint3-deliverables]].

## D6 Mutation testing (new)

- Tool: **StrykerJS with the Vitest runner** (Actual Budget). Hand-made mutations don't count.
- Pick one issue whose PR changes both source and tests; mutate **only the source files changed by that PR** (535: two issues).
- Add `"json"` to Stryker `reporters`. Commit `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json` and `-after.json`, plus the config and command. Reusing a teammate's config is fine if credited, but each student runs it themselves.
- Analyze every survivor (if more than 10, at least 10, starting with lines the PR changed): **equivalent** or **test gap**, and why.
- Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a gap survivor; it must show as killed in the "after" report. Scores quoted in the write-up must match the reports.
- Write-up `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<username>.md`: title `Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <title>`. Header fields: PR(s), Tool, Config (link + credit), Command, Reports (before/after links), Mutation score before% → after%. Surviving mutants table (Location file:line | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why). New or strengthened test (commit link, file › test name, which mutant it kills). Questions: (1) what survivors revealed about the tests; (2) whether any survivor exposed an assertion whose expected value wasn't based on the requirements; (3) AI use and what was verified or corrected, or N/A.
- Rubric: tool run on PR files with config, command, and reports committed 4 · survivors analyzed correctly 4 · a killing test, confirmed by re-run 4 · answers show understanding 3.
- Common problems: tests that already fail on unchanged code stop Stryker, so fix or exclude them; tests that run against `dist` never see the mutants; narrowing the test set can produce fake survivors. If blocked, ask teammates first, then the TA early (with the errors and the AI log).

Extra credit: an upstream PR accepted or under active review (+3 each); an upstream bug report confirmed by maintainers (+2 each).

Related: [[course-site-reference]], [[course-pr-requirements]], [[course-issue-requirements]], [[course-ai-log-rules]].

=== course-ai-log-rules.md
---
name: course-ai-log-rules
description: 'CSCI 435 AI log rules — folder/file naming, required content, SpecStory, and the exact "AI Assistance" issue/PR comment template'
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c234029d-15b4-4a34-81c4-d33c3beb84df
  modified: 2026-11-10T00:18:37.964Z
---

**Why:** graded strictly. Summaries, paraphrased prompts, share links, screenshots, or output without its prompts get no credit, and an unlinked log counts as missing.
**How to apply:** whenever finishing work on an issue or PR, or writing a report's AI section, check the log is real and linked.

- Log **every** AI session on the project: code, debugging, review, understanding code, drafting issues, PRs, or docs, design talk. Unproductive sessions count too. "When in doubt, log it." (Course-admin questions don't need logging.)
- Path: `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<github-username>/` (this user: `tigerk9`). Never put logs in a teammate's folder.
- Name: `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md` (date = session start; lowercase hyphenated). Tool ids: `claude-code`, `claude-web`, `claude-desktop`, `cursor`, `gemini-cli`, `codex-cli`, `copilot`, `chatgpt`, `other-<name>`. Example: `2026-11-08_claude-code_issue-96-implementation.md`.
- Formats: `.md` preferred, `.txt`/`.json` OK. Not `.html`/`.pdf`/`.docx`. Attachments go in a sibling folder named exactly like the log minus `.md`.
- Content: model + tool, the full prompt and response history, and (for agentic tools) every file edit and command. Must be captured at the time, never reconstructed afterwards.
- Capture: run sessions via `specstory run claude`. If one was started without it, `specstory sync` converts local history into `.specstory/history/`. Copy sprint files into the log folder and rename to the convention.
- SpecStory CLI (v2.17.0, checked 2026-11-10 via `--help`) is **not on PATH** in the dev container: plain `specstory` → "command not found". Binary: `/app/.specstory/bin/specstory` (repo copy: `.specstory/bin/specstory`). Run from the repo root. One session: `/app/.specstory/bin/specstory sync claude -s <session-uuid>`; `--print` writes to stdout, `--output-dir <dir>` changes the folder (default `./.specstory/history`), `--local-time-zone` for local timestamps (default UTC). The current Claude Code session's UUID is the last folder of the scratchpad path. Output is named `<UTC start>-<first words>.md`. Sync after the session's last reply (re-running updates the same file).
- Link: one comment per contributor per issue (implementer, reviewer, tester, and estimator each post their own). From S2 on it may go on the issue **or** the PR. It must link the **specific file**, not the folder and not a different issue. Edit the comment to add rows for later sessions. No AI used → still post the comment saying "No AI used" (and the folder must still exist).

Exact template (prefix with 🤖 when the agent posts it):

```
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation / Code review / Testing / Other

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-web | [link](ai-logs/sprint0/jsmith/2026-09-08_claude-web_understanding-issue-42.md) | Understanding the issue, locating relevant code |
| 2 | claude-code | [link](ai-logs/sprint0/jsmith/2026-09-09_claude-code_issue-42-implementation.md) | Implementing the fix and writing tests |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-08_claude-web_understanding-issue-42/](ai-logs/sprint0/jsmith/2026-09-08_claude-web_understanding-issue-42/)
```

Relative links in GitHub comments don't resolve, so use full blob URLs: `https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/blob/master/ai-logs/...`, and make sure the log is pushed or merged first so the link works.

End-of-sprint: `specstory sync` → export web chats → rename → move into the folder → push → confirm every issue/PR touched has a working AI Assistance comment.

Related: [[course-pr-requirements]], [[course-issue-requirements]], [[course-site-reference]].

110	## Requirements & Design
111	
112	**Were specs complete before coding?** For most issues, yes. Feature issues had a user story, user scenario, acceptance criteria and out-of-scope list, and bug issues had observed behavior, expected behavior and steps to reproduce, before work began. The exceptions were #119 and #120, which were created after their PRs to document CI fixes that had to happen immediately to unblock everyone else.
113	
114	**Surprises:**
115	
116	- **The upstream sync was much harder than expected.** It was estimated at 1 point. Merging the `v26.10.0` release tag produced dozens of false conflicts and had to be aborted. The final merge brought in 215 upstream commits and needed 25 conflicts resolved by hand.
117	- **CI had never run on any of our PRs.** Upstream's workflows use Depot runners, which are blocked on our repo. That meant lint errors, 69 outdated screenshots and a broken E2E test had reached master unnoticed.
118	- **#11 was smaller than estimated.** It was first estimated as large. Once we found that the YTD logic and starting balance already existed in `net-worth-spreadsheet.ts`, it was re-scoped to medium.
119	- **#70 found a real bug.** Its new layout tests found a narrow-screen bug between 668 and 749px, filed as [#139](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/issues/139).
120	
121	**Key design decisions.** Full details, including consequences, are in each linked issue or PR.
122	
123	| Issue / PR | Decision | Alternatives considered | Why |
124	| :--------- | :------- | :---------------------- | :-- |
125	| [#53](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/issues/53) / [PR 84](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/84) (sgstrick) | Icon size is its own setting, with fixed Small/Medium/Large options. | Let the user enter an exact size or scale for icons. | Fixed sizes can each be tested to fit in every page layout. An arbitrary size could break layouts. |

Target the upstream commit the 26.10.0 release was built from. | Rebase our commits onto upstream; GitHub's "Sync fork" button; merge the `v26.10.0` tag; merge upstream's latest `master`. | Rebasing would rewrite shared history. 159	## Test Strategy
160	
161	**Getting CI working came first.** Before [PR #113](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/113), CI had never run on our PRs, because upstream's workflows use Depot runners that are blocked on our repo. Lint errors, outdated screenshots and a broken E2E test had reached master as a result. After moving CI to GitHub-hosted runners, we fixed the failures that had piled up:
162	
163	- [PR #115](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/115) fixed lint, formatting and knip errors.
164	- [PR #116](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/116) regenerated 69 outdated VRT screenshots.
165	- [PR #132](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/132) fixed the bug behind the failing "schedules" E2E test.
166	- [PR #104](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/104) fixed tests that failed locally: Windows file locks, Vitest picking up Stryker's leftover `.stryker-tmp` copies, and an i18n race in `mutations.test.tsx`.
167	
168	From then on, every PR got lint, typecheck, unit, E2E and VRT checks automatically.
169	
170	**Kinds of tests written:**
171	
172	- **Unit and component tests (Vitest)** were the most common.
173	  - [PR #84](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/84) tests saving and loading the icon size setting, the default fallback, and the pixel size for each option.
174	  - [PR #128](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/128) adds `subcategories.test.ts` and `showActivity.test.ts`, which check that unchecked subcategories are left out of custom reports.
175	  - [PR #132](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/132) adds three pinned-sidebar tests using fake timers, including a regression test for the original bug, and updates three existing tests.
176	  - [PR #136](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/136) adds six tests for the hex input.
177	  - PRs [#124](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/124) and [#130](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/130) add AI-generated unit tests for the net worth percentage and personal inflation features.
178	- **End-to-end tests (Playwright).**
179	  - [PR #129](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/129) tests bulk skip, complete and delete, select-all, completed rows having no checkbox, and clicking a row still opening the editor.
180	  - [PR #140](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/140) tests layouts at four viewport widths in three themes, plus a sweep across 19 widths. It records two known layout bugs with `test.fail()`, so they become regression tests once fixed.
181	- **Visual regression tests (VRT).** Screenshots were regenerated whenever a PR changed the UI ([PR #116](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/116), [PR #128](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/128), [PR #129](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/129)).
182	- **Mutation testing (Stryker).** In [PR #112](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/112), the changed code scored 100%, and each killed mutant was checked to be a real test failure.
183	
184	**What we couldn't test automatically, and why:**
185	
186	- **Upstream sync ([PR #99](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/99)).** It touched hundreds of files we didn't write, so no new tests could cover it. The author checked the app by hand for regressions and asked teammates to do the same before merging.
187	- **CI changes ([PR #113](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/113)).** A workflow can only be tested by running it on GitHub. We verified it by watching CI run on the PR, and tested the runner-label checker by hand against sample workflows.
188	- **How things look.** Whether icons look right at every size ([PR #84](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/84)) or colors look right in each theme ([PR #136](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/136), [PR #144](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/144)) needs a person to look. VRT screenshots only catch changes, not whether the new look is correct.
189	- **Mutation testing on Windows.** Stryker's Vitest runner ran 0 tests on Windows and parallel runs crashed, so it had to be run one mutant at a time with temporary configs.
190	- **[PR #144](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/144)'s unit tests** couldn't be run in the author's environment because Vitest wouldn't start. They rely on CI.
191	
192	**Every PR was also tested by hand** in the running app. Several ([#128](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/128), [#130](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/130), [#136](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/136), [#144](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/144)) include step-by-step instructions so the reviewer could repeat the check.

224	## Risks & Retrospective
225	
226	### What went well
227	
228	- **15 of 16 issues merged.** The only open PR ([#144](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/144)) is finished apart from a few small requested changes.
229	- **CI works.** Every PR is now checked automatically. Before this sprint, CI had never run on our repo.
230	- **Our fork is current.** It is synced with upstream v26.10.0, and the tests that used to fail locally (including on Windows) now pass.
231	- **Reviews caught real problems.** Five PRs had changes requested before they were approved.
232	
233	### What slowed us down
234	
235	- **Other commitments.** Work for other classes and jobs was the biggest thing slowing us down, which led to a last-minute scramble. 7 of the 16 issues were closed in the last 30 hours of the sprint.
236	- **Unplanned infrastructure work.** Fixing CI and syncing with upstream took far longer than estimated (the upstream sync was estimated at 1 point). Feature PRs couldn't get green checks until it was done.
237	- **Slow CI runners.** GitHub's hosted runners are slower than upstream's Depot runners, so CI runs took longer and some jobs had to be re-run.
238	
239	### What we would do differently in Sprint 3
240	
241	- Start PRs earlier so there is more time for review and for fixing the finer details. With PRs coming in at the last minute, some small details were skipped for the sake of finishing.
242	- Estimate infrastructure work (syncing, CI) more carefully. It turned out to be much larger than it looked.
243	
244	### Risks going forward
245	
246	- **Flaky CI.** Some CI tests occasionally fail because GitHub-hosted runners are much slower than upstream's Depot runners. Re-running a failed job usually passes, but we need to keep an eye on it and fix tests as the slowness comes up.
247	- **Config drift from upstream.** Our CI workflows, `.oxfmtrc.json` and `knip.json` now differ from upstream's, which may cause merge conflicts at the next upstream sync.
248	- **Known narrow-screen bug.** The layout bug found by PR #140 ([#139](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/issues/139)) is still open.
249	
250	## Sprint 3 Plan
251	
252	- Address the review on [PR #144](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/144) and merge it (carryover of [#67](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/issues/67)).
253	- Polish the PDF export ([#97](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/issues/97)). We planned this after Sprint 1 but didn't get to it this sprint.
254	- Show a "(modified)" label on report widgets with unsaved changes ([#125](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/issues/125), [#126](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/issues/126)).
255	- Fix the narrow-viewport layout bug ([#139](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/issues/139)).
256	- Add issues for bringing the UI changes we made in line with the project's "impeccable" design guidelines.
257	- Add screenshot tests for new UI elements that didn't have them before.
258	- Build a reliable way to update screenshots, like upstream's bot, so we no longer have to add and remove a temporary workflow each time.
259

I can't reproduce the page verbatim because of my quoting limits, so this is a close paraphrase that keeps every requirement. Short exact phrases are quoted.

**D1: Sprint Backlog (milestone and scope)**
- Create a "Sprint 3" milestone in GitHub and attach all selected issues to it.
- Minimums: each CSCI 435 member needs at least 2 medium issues (or equivalent story points). Each CSCI 535 member needs at least 2 medium issues plus 1 additional small issue.
- Each issue states its scope (small or medium) and one or two sentences on why, including which components it touches and how much change is expected. The instructor or TA may reclassify an overstated scope.
- One issue may be a hardening issue. Sources include your baseline run, tech debt from the "Introduced" and "Encountered" fields in Sprint 1 and 2 PRs, known bugs, and the upstream issue tracker.
- Hardening issues need evidence of the fix:
  - Bug fix: a test that fails before the fix and passes after.
  - Flaky test: the root cause, plus repeated runs before and after (20 for a unit test, 10 for an E2E test).
  - Broken or missing CI check: links to CI runs before and after.
  - Baseline failures: pass/fail counts before and after, and the cause of each failure group.
  - Regenerating snapshots, reformatting, or silencing a check without fixing its cause counts as small at most.
- Team feature: split it into sub-issues, each with an owner, spec, and scope. Link them to the feature issue, count them toward minimums, and add them to the milestone.

**D8: Sprint Report**
- Use the Sprint 1 D6 format, plus the additions below.
- Suite health (new section):
  - Baseline table for the suites relevant to your team, not the whole repository. For each suite, list the command or CI workflow and the runner's summary line (passed, failed, skipped) at the Sprint 2 tag ("-csci435-s2") and at sprint end. Use CI where available; locally, run only the packages you changed.
  - Group failures by cause (for example, environment-specific, already broken upstream, flaky, or caused by our changes). Link one issue per cause that lists the affected tests.
  - No failures introduced by your team. Any test your changes broke must be fixed by sprint end. Pre-existing failures only need recording and grouping; fixing them is optional and can be a hardening issue.
  - Skipped tests and disabled CI checks require a linked issue and a reason in a code comment.
- Mutation testing: link each member's D6 file.
- Hardening issues: list them and where each came from.
- Carryovers from Sprint 2 and what changed.
- Submit to `docs/sprint3/report.md` (or `.pdf` or `.docx`). If you submit Markdown, confirm it renders on GitHub.

**Report formatting rules**
- Tables and links must display correctly on GitHub, with no escaped pipes or brackets.
- Use the Sprint 3 sections rather than copying a previous report.

**Mutation testing file locations (for D8 links)**
- Each member's file goes at `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<username>.md`.
- Before and after reports go in `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/`.

**D9: Sprint Release**
- Follow the Sprint 1 D7 process.
- Tag with the "-csci435-s3" suffix.
- Create the release after the last Sprint 3 merge so it matches the final state of `main`.
- The release description should summarize the sprint's changes (features, fixes, hardening work), not just restate the tag name.

=================== #160
2:Actual syncs budgets between devices through the sync server using CRDT messages. The client sends its new changes to `/sync`, gets back changes it hasn't seen yet, and compares merkle trees to confirm both sides are in sync. Right now no test checks that whole loop end to end. The client tests in `packages/loot-core/src/server/sync/` (`sync.test.ts`, `sync.property.test.ts`) replace the server with a mock (`packages/loot-core/src/server/tests/mockSyncServer.ts`). The server tests in `packages/sync-server/src/app-sync.test.ts` test the endpoints alone, with no real client. So nothing confirms that two real clients connected to a real sync server end up with the same data. This issue adds integration tests that run a real sync server with two or more client instances, plus scenarios for the cases where multi-device sync usually breaks: edits made at the same time, offline devices, sync resets and encrypted files.

14:   - creates at least two independent client instances pointed at that server

=================== #161
2:Actual syncs budgets between devices through the sync server using CRDT messages. Today no test runs a real client against a real sync server. The client tests in `packages/loot-core/src/server/sync/` replace the server with a mock (`packages/loot-core/src/server/tests/mockSyncServer.ts`), and the server tests in `packages/sync-server/src/app-sync.test.ts` exercise the endpoints with no real client. This issue builds the test setup that end-to-end sync tests need: start the real sync server in-process with temporary storage, create a user and a budget file, and connect two or more independent client instances to it. It also adds helpers to sync a device and compare devices. The scenarios themselves are a separate issue (#162), which depends on this one.

18	## Description
19	
20	<!-- What does this PR do? Why is it needed? Please give context on the "why?": why do we need this change? What problem is it solving for you?-->
21	This PR allows users to dynamically view and select custom colors for their tags, where clicking the color preview next to the hex field will now open a saturation/brightness area and hue slider (react-aria-components), kept in sync with the swatches and hex input through the shared picker state.
22	
23	
24	<!-- If AI tools wrote a significant part of this change, please disclose it here and name the tool you used. See https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing/ai-usage-policy -->
25	This change was written with the help of Claude Code (Anthropic).

27	## Design
28	| Field | Description |
29	|---|---|
30	| Decision | Keep the live preview separate from saving. Every color change is written straight into the cached list of tags, with no database write, so all visible tags recolor live. The color is saved (`updateTag`) only once a change is settled, through a new `onChangeEnd` prop on `ColorPicker`. A change counts as settled when a swatch is picked, a complete hex code is entered, a drag ends, or a held key is released. |
31	| Alternatives Considered | **B:** throttle or debounce `updateTag` to about 150 ms. **C:** an explicit Apply/Cancel button. |
32	| Rationale | Saving on every `onChange` would flood the database and the sync server with writes while dragging, and tags would flicker as refetches overlap. "B" still records intermediate colors in sync history. "C" adds an extra click and behaves differently from swatches, which apply instantly. "A" satisfies the "update in real time with existing tags" acceptance criterion with exactly one save per change. |
33	| Consequences | `ColorPicker` gained a new `onChangeEnd` prop, because react-aria's picker only provides `onChange`. Every keyboard step also counts as a settled change, so held keys had to be batched into a single save on release, and accelerated so they don't feel slow. If the popover closes mid-change, the pending color is saved when the picker closes. |
34

114	## Design decisions
115	
116	### How to tell that a widget has unsaved changes
117	
118	- **Chosen: compare the current settings with the saved widget.** Each report builds its "Save widget" settings with one function, and the label shows when the result differs from the saved `widget.meta` (after filling in the same defaults the page uses when it opens).
119	- **Alternative 1: a "touched" flag** set whenever the user changes any setting, and cleared on save.
120	  - Simpler to add to each page.
121	  - But changing a setting and then changing it back would still show the label, which fails AC3. Every setter on every page would also need to remember to set the flag.
122	- **Alternative 2: block leaving the page with a prompt** instead of showing a label.
123	  - Rejected in #96: it needs changes to `App.tsx` and the router, which is out of scope for this issue.
124	- **Rationale:** comparing with the saved widget is the only option that satisfies AC3. Building the saved and the compared settings from the same function also means a setting can't be saved without being compared, which AC6 tests.
125	- **Consequences:**
126	  - Each report needs a `*WidgetSettings.ts` module, and its comparison has to repeat the defaults the page uses when it opens. Changing one means updating the other (see Tech Debt).
127	  - Each page has to wait until its saved settings have loaded before comparing, so the label doesn't flash while loading (`isRangeReady`).
128	
129	### How to compare relative date ranges
130	
131	- **Chosen: compare the range setting**, not the dates it currently resolves to. Sliding windows compare their length, "All time" and named ranges ("last month", "year to date") compare only the mode, and fixed ranges compare the exact dates.
132	- **Alternative 1: compare the resolved start and end dates.** A widget saved as "last 6 months" would show as modified as soon as a new month starts, without the user changing anything.
133	- **Alternative 2: compare the saved `timeFrame` exactly as stored.** Pages save absolute dates even for sliding windows and re-resolve them when they open, so this has the same problem.
134	- **Rationale:** matches the proposed answer to the issue's first open question, and what "Save widget" would actually change.
135	- **Consequences:** `toComparableTimeFrame` has to know every range mode. It also absorbs Crossover's "move back one month" adjustment when it opens.
136	
137	### Other decisions
138	
139	- The baseline is the saved widget fetched from the server. A successful save refreshes it, so the label disappears; a failed save doesn't, so the label stays.
140	- On Calendar, the date filter added by clicking a day on the dashboard card counts as a change, because "Save widget" would save it.
141	- Renaming a Summary widget now saves only the name. Previously it also saved any unsaved "Show as" changes. This matches the other seven reports.
142	- "Save widget" stays enabled even when nothing has changed (issue's second open question).
143	- Crossover's range adjustment moved into `crossoverWidgetSettings.ts`, so the page and the comparison share it.
144	
145	## Scope:
146	
147	- Included: the eight reports listed above, in both the desktop and mobile headers.
148	- Not included: Formula and the experimental reports (#126), Custom Reports (they already have the label), any prompt when leaving the page, and any change to `App.tsx` or the router.
149	
150	## Tests:
151	
152	- `widgetModified.test.ts`: time-range comparison (each mode, day vs month windows, defaults), filter defaults, and when `isWidgetModified` returns early.
153	- `*WidgetSettings.test.ts` (one per report):
154	  - Compared settings match saved settings, each setting's change is detected, the name is ignored, and empty settings match the defaults.
155	  - Report-specific cases: Spending's live comparisons, Summary's "Show as" content, and Crossover's range adjustment and category/account order.
156	- `GoalReport.test.tsx`, `NetWorth.test.tsx`: the page-level behaviour described above.

194	### Description
195	
196	Upstream's `/update-vrt` comment bot can't run in our fork (its jobs are limited to
197	`actualbudget/actual` and need Depot runners), and screenshots made in our arm64 dev containers
198	don't match CI. The only working way to update VRT screenshots was copying a temporary workflow
199	into the PR (#116). This PR adds a permanent **Update VRT screenshots** workflow that anyone can
200	start from the Actions tab with a PR number.
201	
202	- **`.github/workflows/update-vrt.yml` (new).** Checks the PR is open and from this repo, builds it
203	  and runs VRT with `--update-snapshots=changed` in CI's container (`playwright:v1.61.1-jammy`,
204	  same build steps as `e2e-test.yml`), then pushes one commit with only the changed PNGs and starts
205	  E2E Tests on it. Optional "Test files" input runs only those files in one shard. The jobs that run
206	  the PR's code only get a read-only token; the job that pushes never runs PR code and re-checks
207	  that every file is a PNG in a `*-snapshots` folder.
208	- **`e2e-test.yml`:** `workflow_dispatch` trigger, so the workflow can start the checks on its commit.
209	- **`e2e-vrt-comment.yml`:** replaces "comment `/update-vrt`" with step-by-step instructions and
210	  the failed test files, read from the VRT JUnit reports by `.github/scripts/vrt-failed-files.mjs`.
211	- **`fork-ci-guard.yml`:** also runs the tests in `.github/scripts` (lage only runs workspace tests).
212	- **`STUDENTS.md`:** new "Updating VRT screenshots" section.
213	- Release note
214	
215	AI disclosure: written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5); see the AI Assistance comment for the log.
216	
217	### Design decisions
218	
219	The issue's Design section (icsasso) chose a new `workflow_dispatch` workflow over adapting
220	upstream's `/update-vrt`. These are the decisions I made while implementing it.
221	
222	**1. How the checks run on the bot's screenshot commit**
223	
224	- **Decision:** after pushing, the workflow starts E2E Tests on the PR branch itself with
225	  `workflow_dispatch`, which needed a `workflow_dispatch:` trigger in `e2e-test.yml`.
226	- **Alternatives considered:**
227	  1. _Re-run the old VRT check by hand_ (the issue's original AC 3). Doesn't work: a re-run tests
228	     the same commit as the original run, so it tests the old screenshots.
229	  2. _Push an empty commit or close and reopen the PR by hand._ Works and changes no upstream file,
230	     but every person has to remember an extra step after each update.
231	  3. _A personal access token secret_ so the bot's push starts CI. Needs a repo admin to create
232	     and rotate a token tied to one person's account.
233	- **Rationale:** `workflow_dispatch` is the one event GitHub lets `GITHUB_TOKEN` start, so it needs
234	  no secret and no manual step. The cost is three lines in one upstream file.
235	- **Consequences:** _Easier:_ the checks start on their own after an update. _Harder:_ one more
236	  upstream edit that can conflict at syncs; branches made before this merges can't be started this
237	  way (the workflow warns and says to merge `master`); and GitHub still holds the other PR checks
238	  for approval, so E2E can run twice.
239	
240	**2. Which job gets write access**
241	
242	- **Decision:** split the workflow so the jobs that build and run the PR's code (`build-web`,
243	  `generate`) have a read-only token, and only the `commit` job can push. It never runs PR code: it
244	  re-checks the downloaded files are PNG screenshots, then commits and pushes.
245	- **Alternatives considered:**
246	  1. _One job that runs the tests and pushes_ (like #116's temporary workflow). Simpler, but the
247	     PR's code would run with a token that can push to any branch.
248	  2. _Upstream's two-workflow design_ (generate a patch, then a separate `workflow_run` workflow
249	     applies it). Same separation, but two files, and `workflow_run` workflows can only be tested
250	     after they're on `master`.
251	- **Rationale:** keeps the separation upstream uses, in one file that could be tested on a fork
252	  before merging.
253	- **Consequences:** _Easier:_ a broken or malicious test can't push anything but screenshots.
254	  _Harder:_ screenshots move between jobs as artifacts, and the PNG check runs in two places.
255	
256	### Related issue(s)

429	## Tech Debt
430	
431	**Introduced:**
432	- **`createTag()` submits with the "Add" button instead of Enter.** This works around #183 (pressing Enter drops the typed description). As a result, the Enter path has no e2e test. Once #183 is fixed, `createTag()` should go back to pressing Enter.
433	- **The color picker is found by what it contains.** The picker's dialog has no accessible name or test id, so `TagsPage.colorPicker` matches the dialog that holds the "Hex color" field. If that field is renamed, the locator breaks. Adding an `aria-label` to the dialog in `ColorPicker.tsx` would be a cleaner fix, but this PR doesn't change production code.
434	- **Swatches are picked by position.** `pickSwatch(6)` relies on the order of `DEFAULT_COLOR_SET`, because the swatches' accessible names are generated color descriptions, not hex values. If the color set is reordered, the swatch test's expected value (`#1976D2`) has to change with it.
435	- **The hue-slider test only checks that the color changed and stayed changed after a reload.** It doesn't check the exact resulting color, because that depends on react-aria's step size. A regression that moves the hue the wrong way would still pass.
436	- **Workarounds for hover and pressed states in the page model**
437	  - `pressCustomColorButton()` uses the keyboard so the hover tooltip doesn't appear.
438	  - `moveMouseAway()` avoids the hover color mix.
439	  - Colors are checked after the popover closes, to avoid the darker pressed style.
440	  - The screenshot test sets the viewport to 1280×900 so the expanded picker isn't cut off.
441	
442	  Each workaround has a comment in the code, but all of them depend on how the UI currently behaves.
443	
444	**Encountered:**
445	- **Losing the description on Enter (#183):** a production bug that these tests uncovered. I filed it and worked around it rather than fixing it, to keep this PR test-only.
446	- **Missing accessibility hooks in `ColorPicker`:** the dialog has no label, and the swatches have no labels a test can match exactly. This caused the locator and swatch-position workarounds above. I left it as is.
447	- **The "Pick a custom color" tooltip:** it covers the color area and swallows the next Escape key press, which broke the screenshots and closing the picker. I worked around it in the page model instead of changing the tooltip.
448	- **Generating screenshots needs a workaround:** they have to come from CI's Linux Playwright container, and the repo has no built-in way to generate them for a PR. I used a temporary workflow, as in PR #116, then removed it and squashed its commits out of the history.

## Description

Adds a test setup for end-to-end sync tests: a real sync server and two or more real clients ("devices") in one test, with helpers to change, sync and compare devices. Until now no test ran a real client against a real server. The loot-core sync tests use `mockSyncServer.ts`, and `app-sync.test.ts` tests the server endpoints with no client. This setup is the groundwork for the sync scenarios in #162.

**What's included** (all in `packages/sync-server/integration-tests/`):

- **Server:** `startSyncServer()` starts the real sync-server app in the test process on a free port, with temporary `serverFiles`/`userFiles`. `startSyncServerWithBudget()` also creates the account, logs in, and uploads a starter budget, returning `token`, `fileId` and `groupId`. `shutdown()` stops the server and deletes its directories.
- **Devices:** `createDevice()` gives each client its own worker thread and data directory, so devices don't share prefs, clock or database. Each device is a full loot-core client through `@actual-app/api`.
- **Helpers:** `makeChange`, `sync`, `goOffline`/`goOnline`, `assertInSync`, plus `setUpTwoDevices()` for the common case. Devices only talk to loopback hosts and never sync on their own, so tests decide exactly when data moves.
- **Tests:** 13 tests in 8 files, including the smoke test (a change on A shows up on B after both sync).
- **README:** how to write a scenario, the helper reference, and answers to the issue's open questions.

**Changes outside the new folder:**

- `sync-server/src/app.ts` exports its Express `app` (one line), and `package.json` gets a matching `#app` subpath import, so tests can listen on port 0 and close the server afterwards.
- `sync-server`'s `test` script runs the unit tests and then the new `test:integration` script. `typecheck` also checks `integration-tests/`.
- `sync-server/vitest.config.ts` excludes `integration-tests/` from the unit-test run.
...

87	## Design Decisions
88	
89	1. **One worker thread per device.** loot-core keeps its clock, database, prefs and sync state in module-level variables, so each device needs its own module graph.
90	   - Alternatives considered: (a) several clients in one module graph, separated with `vi.resetModules()`; (b) a child process per device.
91	   - Why: (a) still shares globals such as `fetch` and the SQLite handles, and depends on Vitest's module cache. (b) works but starts more slowly and needs a separate entry script and inter-process messaging. Worker threads are isolated by construction and start quickly.
92	   - Consequence: devices are controlled through messages (`device.request(...)`), and changes and results must be plain data.
93	
94	2. **Clients go through the bundled `@actual-app/api`.**
95	   - Alternatives considered: (a) loot-core's internal modules directly; (b) a new client entry point inside loot-core.
96	   - Why: the API already supports `init` with a server URL and session token, and `downloadBudget`. Its bundle runs in a plain worker thread, which loot-core's TypeScript source can't, and (b) would change loot-core code, which the issue wanted to avoid.
97	   - Consequence: the API has to be built before the tests (lage does this), and devices use the API's build, not loot-core source.
98	
99	3. **The setup lives in `packages/sync-server/integration-tests/`.**
100	   - Alternatives considered: (a) a new test-only workspace (the first version of this PR); (b) inside loot-core.
101	   - Why: (a) changes `yarn.lock`, which triggers the Dependency Review check that can't run in this fork. (b) would make loot-core depend on the server.
102	   - Consequence: sync-server doesn't list `@actual-app/api` as a dependency, so devices load `packages/api/dist/index.js` by path with hand-written types (see Tech Debt), and the starter budget is zipped without a zip library.
103	
104	4. **The tests run on every `yarn test`.**
105	   - Alternatives considered: (a) only a separate `yarn test:integration` script; (b) a separate CI job.
106	   - Why: they take about 30 seconds, and if they don't run by default they stop being run. `test:integration` is still there for running them alone.
107	   - Consequence: `sync-server`'s tests now wait for the API build, which lage caches.
108	
109	5. **Devices never sync on their own.** The worker wraps `fetch`: it blocks automatic syncs, simulates being offline, and refuses non-loopback hosts.
110	   - Alternatives considered: (a) let loot-core's 1-second auto-sync run and wait for it; (b) use fake timers.
111	   - Why: (a) makes tests timing-dependent. (b) doesn't work across worker threads, and loot-core's sync also waits on real I/O.
112	   - Consequence: tests must call `sync()` explicitly. Workers run with `NODE_ENV=production`, because in test mode loot-core syncs inside every change and throws when that fails.
113	
114	## Tech Debt
115	
116	**Introduced:**
117	
118	- **Hand-written API types.** Devices load the built API by its path in the repo (`packages/api/dist/index.js`), and `apiBundle.ts` declares the API methods they call. These types aren't checked against the real API, so a change to one of those signatures won't fail typecheck; it would show up as a test failure. This avoids adding a dependency (and a `yarn.lock` change).
119	- **Own zip writer.** `zip.ts` writes uncompressed zip files so the tests don't need a zip library. It's test-only and small.
120	- **Vitest temp folder cleanup.** `integration-tests/vitest.globalSetup.ts` removes temp folders Vitest 5 leaves behind on Windows, using Vitest's internal `_tmpDir`. It only deletes folders directly under the OS temp directory, so if Vitest changes, it does nothing instead of deleting the wrong thing.
121	- **Possible leftover temp folder.** If a test times out while the server or a device is still starting up, that temporary directory isn't removed.
122	- **Only account changes.** `makeChange` supports account create/update/delete. More change types (transactions, categories) will be added in #162; the README explains how.
123	- **Workers run with `NODE_ENV=production`** to avoid loot-core's test-mode sync behavior (see Design Decision 5).

127	- **`yarn typecheck` overwrites the API build.** `packages/api/tsconfig.json` emits JavaScript, so a typecheck replaces the bundled `packages/api/dist/index.js` with an unbundled compile that devices can't load. Handled: lage rebuilds the API before `sync-server`'s tests, and the integration tests stop at once with "run `yarn build:api`" if the bundle is missing or overwritten. Not fixed here, because the fix belongs in the API package.
128	- **Dependency Review can't run in this fork.** The dependency graph isn't enabled, so any PR that changes `yarn.lock` fails. Handled by not changing `yarn.lock` (Design Decision 3).

132	- **sync-server's `app.ts` didn't export `app`,** so it could only be started through `run()` on a fixed port. Added the export.

181	## Design decisions
182	
183	### What the label compares against when a report saves from more than one place
184	
185	- **Chosen: the saved widget from the query cache, with every write going through `useUpdateDashboardWidgetMutation`.** The mutation refreshes the cache after any successful save, so Save widget, rename, or a future write site all keep the label correct without extra bookkeeping. This matches #125.
186	- **Alternative 1: a local "last saved" snapshot updated in each save handler.** Every write site would have to remember to update it; missing one leaves the label stuck. It also duplicates state the cache already holds.
187	- **Alternative 2: write the new settings into the cache directly (optimistic update) at each save site.** Same "every site must remember" problem, plus rollback logic for failed saves.
188	- **Consequences:** Balance Forecast's save had to move onto the mutation. Any future write site must use it too. The label clears when the refreshed widget arrives, a moment after the save succeeds.
189	
190	### Leaving computed values out of the Monte Carlo comparison
191	
192	- **Chosen: compare user inputs only.** Both sides are read through `monteCarloConfigFromMeta`, and `startingBalance` is dropped for pots linked to an account.
193	- **Alternative 1: compare everything.** The label would appear whenever a linked account's balance changes.
194	- **Alternative 2: stop saving linked balances.** Out of scope, and the dashboard card uses them as a fallback while live balances load.

208	## Description
209	
210	Lets users attach receipts and other files (JPEG, PNG, WebP or PDF, up to 10 MB) to transactions. As rescoped for this sprint, files are stored **on this device only**: they are not uploaded to the sync server, and the attachments table is not synced. Server storage is left for a follow-up issue.
211	
212	- **Data layer (loot-core):**
213	  - A new `transaction_attachments` table (migration `1794608098000_add_transaction_attachments.sql`) has a `storage` column (always `'local'` for now), so server storage can be added later without another migration.
214	  - Files are saved at `<budgetDir>/attachments/<id>` through the existing file-system layer, so storage works the same in Electron and the browser. Each file is written to a temporary file, then renamed. The fs layer had no `rename`, so one was added for Electron, the browser (moves the IndexedDB record in one transaction) and the API.
215	  - Handlers: `attachment-add`, `attachment-remove`, `attachment-list`, `attachment-read`. Rows are written with `db.runQuery`, not `db.insert`, so they never produce sync messages. Add and remove send a `sync-event` so live queries refresh.
216	  - The size, empty-file and type checks live in `shared/attachments.ts`, so the UI and the backend use the same rules. The type is decided from the file's first bytes, never from the file name or the type the browser reports.
217	- **Export, import and upload:** Export includes the `attachments/` folder. Import restores it, and every imported file goes through the same checks as a new attachment. The budget snapshot uploaded to the server has the attachments table cleared, so a second device doesn't get rows without files.
218	- **Split transactions:** attachments belong to the parent. A split child's request goes to its parent, so files survive splitting and unsplitting.

280	## Design decisions
281	
282	### Storing attachments on this device only
283	
284	- **Chosen: files in the budget folder; rows written without sync messages; the table cleared in the snapshot uploaded to the server.** This was the agreed rescope of #154: server storage was about a third of the original scope, and neither #155 nor #156 builds it.
285	- **Alternative 1: sync the rows but not the files.** Other devices would get rows pointing at files they don't have, so every attachment would show as missing there.
286	- **Alternative 2: upload files to the sync server now.** Too much for one sprint, and it needs server-side work (storage, quotas, cleanup).
287	- **Consequences:** a `storage` column is already in the table, so server storage can be added without another migration. Known gaps, left for #155 or a follow-up:
288	  - Re-downloading the budget from the server replaces `db.sqlite`, so the rows disappear while the files stay on disk.
289	  - `duplicate-budget` doesn't copy `attachments/`.
290	  - Local backups don't include attachment files.
291	
292	### Attachments on a split go on the parent
293	
294	- **Chosen: the parent only; a child's request is sent to its parent.** Splitting keeps the parent's id, so files survive splitting and unsplitting.
295	- **Alternative: allow attachments on children.** Unsplitting deletes the children, so their files would need to be moved or would be lost.
296	- **Consequences:** child rows never show the paperclip. Opening attachments from a child shows the parent's.
297	
298	### Opening PDFs
299	
300	- **Chosen: in the browser, open the PDF in a new tab from the viewer; in the desktop app, offer "Save a copy".** Electron only lets `window.open` reach external URLs, so it can't open a file held in memory in a new window.
301	- **Alternative 1: open the tab directly when the PDF is clicked.** The file has to load first, and opening a tab after waiting gets blocked as a pop-up.
302	- **Alternative 2: show the PDF inside the viewer in an `<iframe>`.** This depends on the browser's or Electron's PDF plugin, which isn't reliably available.
303	- **Consequences:** in the browser, opening a PDF takes two clicks: the file name, then "Open in new tab".
304

115	## Description
116	
117	This PR adds a Transactions column to the Manage Tags page that shows how many transactions use each tag, allowing users to find unused tags at a glance and clean up their tag list.

122	
123	Closes #148

125	## Design Decision: Matching "View Transactions" counts
126	
127	Each count must equal what View Transactions (the `hasTags` filter) lists.
128	
129	**Alternative 1: Run the `hasTags` query once per tag.** Matches by
130	construction, but it's one full scan per tag. Also, `$count` on grouped
131	transactions counts split children separately instead of once per split.
132	
133	**Alternative 2: One scan with a tokenizer.** Fastest, but it's a second copy
134	of the matching rules that could silently drift from `hasTags`.
135	
136	**Chosen: One scan with a shared pattern.** I moved the regex into
137	`tagMatchPattern()`, used by both `hasTags` and the new counts handler. One
138	query fetches tagged notes, grouped by split. Each tag's pattern is then tested
139	in memory, which is fine for the expected ≤100 tags. This keeps a single source
140	of matching rules at the cost of one query. A test compares every count with the
141	real View Transactions query.

163	## Tech Debt
164	
165	**Introduced:**
166	- **Split and deleted-row logic is copied, not shared.** The counts query copies the grouped transaction list's rules: it reads `v_transactions_internal_alive` and groups split children under their parent with `IFNULL(parent_id, id)`. It doesn't call that code directly. A test compares every count with the real View Transactions query, so the two can't drift apart unnoticed.
167	- **Counting work grows with the number of tags.** Each tag's pattern is checked against every tagged note in JS, roughly tags × tagged notes regex checks. That's fine for the expected ≤100 tags; budgets with many more tags would need a single-pass approach instead.
168	- **Counts reload every time the Tags page opens** (`staleTime: 0`). That's simpler than refreshing them precisely after each transaction edit, but it costs one extra query per visit.
169	- **An invisible copy of the View Transactions button sits in the header.** The button column is sized to its content, so the hidden copy keeps the new column aligned at any translated button width, instead of giving the button a fixed width.
170	
171	**Encountered:**
172	- **`hasTags` and `hasAnyTag` each had their own copy of the regex escaping.**
173	  I merged them into a shared `tagMatchPattern()`, which now also drives the counts.
174	- **The rules engine (`condition.ts`) has a third, lowercased copy of the tag
175	  regex.** Its case-insensitive matching is intentionally different, so I left it alone (out of scope).
176	- **The Tags table header didn't account for the list's scrollbar width.**
177	  This only showed once a right-aligned column existed. I fixed it with `Table`'s existing `saveScrollWidth` callback.
178	- **`main.test.ts > budget is successfully loaded` times out locally** (~6 s against a 5 s limit). It fails the same way on the code before this branch, so I left it unchanged.
179	- **Checking only changed files is awkward.** `tsc-strict` rejects file arguments with the current TypeScript (TS5112), and desktop-client's typecheck reads loot-core's built `@types`, which go stale until rebuilt with `tsgo -b`. I worked around both by checking whole packages.

2	## Description
3	
4	Adds attachments to the mobile layout, and defines what happens to attachments when a transaction, account or budget is deleted, when a delete is undone, and when transactions are merged. It also cleans up attachment files on the device that nothing uses anymore. Storage stays **on this device only**, as in #154. Syncing attachments and server storage are left for the server-storage follow-up issue.
5	
6	- **Data layer (loot-core):**
7	  - A new `deleted_at` column on `transaction_attachments` (migration `1794882866000_add_attachment_deleted_at.sql`). It's null while the attachment is live.
8	  - `attachment-remove` now soft-removes: it sets `tombstone = 1, deleted_at = now` and keeps the file. Removing twice still succeeds.
9	  - New `attachment-restore` handler. It brings a removed attachment back if its file is still on the device and its transaction isn't deleted. It returns `not-found` or `transaction-not-found` otherwise, and sends a `sync-event` so the open list refreshes.
10	  - A deleted transaction's attachments are hidden everywhere: counts, the paperclip, the attachments list, `attachment-list` and `attachment-read`. Nothing is changed on delete, so undoing the delete brings them back. (The modal's list query already joined live transactions only. That now has a regression test.)
11	  - Export leaves out removed attachments, both rows and files.
12	- **Merging:** the kept transaction gets the attachments of both (`moveAttachments` in `attachments/app.ts`, called from `mergeTransactionsNoTransfer`). This covers merged transfers too. If the kept transaction is a split child, the attachments go to its parent.
13	- **Cleanup on this device** (`server/attachments/cleanup.ts`):
14	  - Runs after a budget opens, without blocking it (fire-and-forget at the end of `_loadBudget`, after checking the same budget is still open). It also runs after an import. There is no timer. An `attachments-cleanup` handler runs it on demand.
15	  - Grace period: **30 days** (`ATTACHMENT_GRACE_MS`).
16	  - Steps, in an order that is safe to interrupt:
17	    1. Stamp `deleted_at` on attachments whose transaction is deleted, and clear it when the delete is undone. Removed attachments keep the time they were removed.
18	    2. Delete rows past the grace period, rows first, then their files.
19	    3. Remove files that no row points to, once they have had no row for the full grace period. First sightings are recorded in `attachments/.cleanup.json`, because the browser file system has no modified time.
20	    4. Remove leftover `.tmp` files the next time cleanup finds them, so a save in progress never loses its temporary file.
21	  - A live attachment on a live transaction is never touched. Neither is a name that isn't an attachment id. Each step logs and carries on if it fails.
22	- **Accounts and budgets:** no code change was needed. Deleting an account deletes its transactions, so their attachments are hidden and then cleaned up like any other delete. Closing an account without deleting its transactions leaves attachments alone. `delete-budget` already removes the budget folder, `attachments/` included. Both have tests now.
23	- **Undo after removing:** after a confirmed removal, a notification says `Removed "<file name>".` with an **Undo** button for 10 seconds. Undo can be pressed while the attachments window is still open, and pressing it doesn't close the window. The confirmation text now says the removal can be undone. If restoring fails, an error notification gives the reason. A failed removal shows no Undo.
24	- **Notifications above modals:** notifications used to be drawn just below modals (`MODAL_Z_INDEX - 1`), so a notification's button couldn't be pressed while a modal was open. The notifications layer is now drawn above modals and marked `data-react-aria-top-layer`. That attribute is how react-aria's own toasts work: the modal leaves the layer out of its inert background, lets focus move into it, and doesn't close when it's clicked. This applies to every notification, not just Undo.
25	- **Mobile transaction list:** rows with attachments show a paperclip before the payee name, labelled "N attachments" for screen readers. Counts come from the same grouped query as desktop, called once per list. Split children and upcoming schedule rows never show one. This covers every mobile screen that shows a transaction list.

27	  - A new "Attachments" field ("None", "1 file", "N files") between Notes and "Delete transaction". It shows on saved transactions only, and on the parent of a split. It opens the same attachments window as desktop.

29	  - The footer and the viewer's buttons wrap on narrow screens. Images in the viewer fit the screen width. PDFs open in a new tab, as in the desktop browser.

88	## Design decisions
89	
90	### Undo for removing an attachment
91	
92	- **Chosen: an "Undo" button in the notification after a removal, backed by a soft remove and `attachment-restore`.** Attachment rows are written without sync messages (#154), and the app's undo stack only records sync messages, so Ctrl/Cmd+Z can't see them.
93	- **Alternative: put attachment changes on the app's undo stack.** That means writing the rows through sync messages, which the server-storage issue will rework anyway.
94	- **Consequences:** Ctrl/Cmd+Z doesn't undo a removal; the notification's Undo does, for 10 seconds. The issue text still says "the app's normal undo" and should be updated.
95	
96	### Notifications above modals
97	
98	- **Chosen: draw the whole notifications layer above modals, marked `data-react-aria-top-layer`.** People remove files inside the attachments window, so Undo has to work while it's open. Raising the z-index alone isn't enough: react-aria makes everything outside an open modal inert, and closes the modal on a click outside it. Both skip top-layer elements.
99	- **Alternative: show Undo inside the attachments window.** That fixes only this one window and duplicates the notification's timeout and error handling.
100	- **Consequences:** every notification now shows above modals, so errors raised while a modal is open are no longer hidden behind it. On a phone, a notification can cover the bottom of a tall modal until it times out or is swiped away.
101	
102	### When files are removed
103	
104	- **Chosen: 30 days after the delete or removal, tracked with a `deleted_at` stamp on the row.** The app's own undo history is cleared every time a budget opens, so the grace period isn't for that. It covers deletes that arrive by sync from another device, and re-downloading a budget, which replaces the rows but leaves the files.
105	- **Alternative: work out delete times from `messages_crdt`.** More complicated, and it doesn't cover attachment rows, which don't sync.
106	- **Consequences:** a deleted transaction's files take up space for 30 days. Files with no row wait 30 days too, which keeps a re-download from losing them the same day.
107	
108	### When cleanup runs
109	
110	- **Chosen: after the budget opens, without blocking it.** Next to the backup service would have been the obvious place, but that only runs outside the browser, and mobile runs in the browser.
111	- **Alternative: a timer.** It adds a moving part for little gain, since budgets are opened often.
112	- **Consequences:** a budget that is never reopened is never cleaned up.
113	
114	### Merging
115	
116	- **Chosen: move the dropped transaction's attachments to the kept one, before the rest of the merge.** The merge isn't one database transaction, so a failure partway leaves things half done either way. Moving first means a failed merge leaves the attachments on the kept transaction, which is still live. Moving last would risk leaving them on the dropped transaction after it was deleted, and cleanup would then remove them after the grace period.
117	- **Alternative: leave them on the dropped transaction.** They would be hidden, then removed after the grace period, so the user would lose them.
118	- **Consequences:** undoing a merge brings the dropped transaction back, but its attachments stay on the kept one, because the undo stack can't see attachment rows. Nothing is lost by the undo itself. But if the user then deletes the kept transaction, both sets of attachments are removed after the grace period.
119

151	## Description
152	
153	Adds end-to-end sync scenario tests: real clients syncing through a real sync server, for the cases where devices usually fall out of step. Until now the client sync tests only ran against a mocked server (`mockSyncServer.ts`), so a change to the client or server sync code could break real multi-device sync without any test failing. Each scenario runs real loot-core devices against the real sync server and ends with `assertInSync`.
154	
155	All scenarios are in `packages/sync-server/integration-tests/src/scenarios/`:
156	
157	1. **Basic sync** (`basicSync.test.ts`): a change on A reaches B, and a change on B reaches A.
158	2. **Same-field conflict** (`conflictSameField.test.ts`): A and B rename the same account before either syncs, and both keep the rename with the later CRDT timestamp. The test reads the real timestamps from the sync results instead of assuming which device wins. Its comment explains how `compareMessages` picks the winner and what happens when timestamps are identical.
159	3. **Different records at the same time** (`conflictDifferentRecords.test.ts`): each device creates and deletes its own account and transaction, and both end up with every tombstone.
160	4. **Offline catch-up** (`offlineCatchUp.test.ts`): B makes 150 accounts (1,050 changes) offline and syncs with no `out-of-sync` error. The comment records how close this gets to `upload.fileSizeSyncLimitMB`. The over-the-limit case is skipped and tracked in #186.
161	5. **Sync reset** (`syncReset.test.ts`): after A resets, B's sync is refused with `file-has-reset` and B applies nothing. After B downloads the budget again, the two are back in sync.
162	6. **Encryption** (`encryption.test.ts`): scenarios 1 and 2 with end-to-end encryption, plus a device with the wrong password, which gets `decrypt-failure` instead of opening the budget.
163	
164	Supporting changes to the test setup from #161:
165	
166	- **Transactions:** devices can create, update and delete transactions. `addTransactions` doesn't return ids, so the worker finds the new one by comparing the account's transactions before and after.
167	- **Encryption:** `startSyncServerWithBudget`, `setUpTwoDevices` and `createDevice` accept an `encryptionPassword`. `src/encryption.ts` encrypts the starter budget with loot-core's scheme and registers the key with the server.
168	- **New helpers:**
169	  - `resetSync` and `downloadBudget`, for the reset scenario;
170	  - `findReceived`, to read the timestamp of a message a device received;
171	  - `countEncryptedServerMessages`, to check what the server stores;
172	  - a `syncRequestBytes` op, to measure upload sizes.
173	- **`assertInSync`:** now reads each device's current group id and encryption key id from its prefs. Without that it couldn't check devices after a sync reset, or devices with an encrypted budget.
174	- **Setup fixes:** `startSyncServer` cleans up even if shutdown fails, and `setUpTwoDevices` stops the server even if a device fails to close. The API bundle check moved into `src/apiBundle.ts` and runs before each device starts. The integration tests' tsconfig is referenced from the root `tsconfig.json`.

181	## Related issue(s)
182	
183	Closes [https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/issues/162]
184	Related to #161 (the test setup this builds on) and #186 (upload batching, found by the offline catch-up scenario)
185	
186	## Testing
187	
188	Every behavioral change has a test:
189	
190	| Change | Tests |
191	| --- | --- |
192	| Scenarios 1–6 | `src/scenarios/*.test.ts`: 12 passing, 1 skipped |
193	| Transaction change types | `transactions.sync.test.ts`: create on A, appears on B; update and delete cross devices |
194	| Encrypted setup | `encryptedBudget.test.ts`: server holds only ciphertext; correct password reads and syncs; wrong password gives `decrypt-failure` |
195	| `assertInSync` 10-row limit | new case in `assertInSync.test.ts` |
196	| Setup and cleanup changes | `startSyncServer.test.ts` (double `shutdown()`, second server refused), `startSyncServerWithBudget.test.ts` (all returned fields) |
197	
198	Strategy:
199	
200	- **Real code, no mocks.** Each test file starts the real sync server on a free port. Each device is a real loot-core client in its own worker thread. Devices only sync when a test tells them to, and they can only reach loopback addresses.
201	- **Outcomes, not implementation.** Tests check what the user and server see: rows, tombstones, merkle hashes, stored messages and error reasons. Where the result depends on CRDT timestamps, the tests read the real timestamps rather than assuming an order.
202	- **Known limitations are skipped, not left failing.** The over-the-limit catch-up is skipped with the expected behavior, the cause and a link to #186.
203	
204	Results:
205	
206	- **Integration suite:** 16 files, 31 passing and 1 skipped. That's 50–60 s on Windows, and 52–55 s in a Linux container (Node 24.18.1, 4 CPUs, approximating CI's `ubuntu-latest`).
207	- **Other checks:** `yarn typecheck` passes. In `yarn test`, every test outside this suite passes except two timeouts in loot-core's `executors.test.ts` while the machine was busy; that file passes on its own and isn't changed here.
208	- **Not yet run on GitHub CI.**
209	- **Windows note:** start the tests from a working directory with an upper-case drive letter (see the README's Troubleshooting section).
210	
211	## Design Decisions
212	
213	- **Encrypting the test budget:** the test server encrypts the starter budget with its own copy of loot-core's scheme (`src/encryption.ts`). The alternatives were having device A turn encryption on through loot-core's `key-make` handler, or checking in pre-encrypted budget files. I chose the copy because the budget is uploaded before any device exists, `key-make` would add a sync reset to every encrypted setup, and fixed files would hide changes to the key format. The consequence is that `src/encryption.ts` has to be kept in step with loot-core: if the scheme changes, encrypted tests fail with `decrypt-failure` until it's updated.
214	- **Offline catch-up size:** the test uses 150 accounts. I considered 500 (the issue's example) and a batch just under the 20 MB limit (about 23,500 accounts). 150 is the smallest count that makes loot-core apply the batch in more than one 100-row chunk, and it keeps the suite under a minute: 500 took 20–38 s on its own, and the near-limit batch would take about 16 minutes. The consequence is that the test doesn't approach the size limit; that's left to the skipped test and #186.
215	- **How `assertInSync` finds the current group and key:** it reads each device's group id and key id from its prefs. The alternatives were updating each device's `connection` after a reset, or adding a separate assertion for reset and encrypted cases. Prefs are where loot-core keeps the real values, so they can't fall out of date, and one assertion covers every scenario. As a result, devices in different groups or with different keys now fail with an `OutOfSyncError` that says so.
216

222	- Each test file starts its own server (about 3 s), because sync-server reads its config once per module graph. With 16 files, the suite is close to the 60 s target. Adding many more scenario files would mean letting files share a server.
223	- The `groupId` guard in `_fullSync` (a sync response arriving after the device's own group changed) isn't tested. It needs a sync request held open while the same device resets.

237	=================== pr189
238	
239	## Description
240	
241	The Payees table showed only names and rule counts, so you couldn't tell which duplicate payee to keep or which ones were stale without opening each one. Now there's:
242	- **Server:** a new query returns each payee's transaction count and last-used date. It reads the same data as the "Show unused payees" filter, so deleted transactions are left out and merged payees count toward their target.
243	- **UI:** new **Transactions** and **Last Used** columns. Payees with no transactions show `0` / `Never` in muted text, and `…` shows while loading.
244	- **Refresh:** the counts and the unused-payees list reload together after a merge, an undo or a sync. This also fixed two existing gaps: undo used to ignore transaction changes, and merges updated the unused list by guessing on the client instead of asking the server.
245	- **Tests, mutation testing reports and a release note.**
246	🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
247	## Design
248	
249	**Decision:** keep the unused-payees list and the new counts as two queries that read the same data, and always reload them together. This was the issue's main risk: the numbers had to agree with the unused filter and with merged payees.
250	
251	**Alternatives:**
252	- **One combined server call:** guaranteed consistency, but it means changing the existing unused-payees code, which is a bigger and riskier change.
253	- **Work out "unused" from the counts on the client:** this would quietly change what "unused" means (e.g. payees referenced by rules), and that's out of scope.
254	- **Count from a different query:** this would duplicate the rules for deleted and merged rows, and risk the two disagreeing.
255	
256	**Trade-off:** the two queries can briefly disagree while one has reloaded and the other hasn't.
257	
258	## Tech Debt
259	
260	**Introduced:**
261	- **Counting logic is in SQL.** It's faster, but mutation testing can't check it, so the server tests are its only protection.
262	- **Speed on large budgets wasn't measured,** and there's no database index for the payee lookup.
263	- **The two queries can briefly disagree** (the trade-off above).
264	- **Translations:** the rules column width fits English labels; a longer translation can misalign a row.
265	- **The refresh logic has no automated tests.**
266	- **Stryker configs and the merge script are course-only files.**

268	**Encountered:**

270	- **Two existing gaps in the Payees page's refresh logic** (undo, merge) were fixed here because they affected the new columns.
271	- **Left alone:** older files that skip strict type-checking, some existing lint warnings, and the "1 associated rules" wording.
